blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Research taste, the judgment of what to read, which problems to pursue, and which methods to try, increasingly shapes the work of AI scientists, yet it remains far less understood than their ability to execute research. We introduce IdeaTaste, a benchmark that scores an LLM by how closely the research proposals it writes from a literature snapshot frozen at 2025 match the work the same communities published in 2026. Our experiments span six contemporary language models and four research areas from established to emerging fields, covering more than 90{,}000 proposals in total. LLM agents fall well short of human communities in both the literature they cite and the ideas they state, reaching about 26\% of the human level on citation matching and only 18\% on idea matching. Their populations can cite as diversely as a community and take up its tasks and methods, yet rarely arrive at the concrete approaches and research plans it pursues. Neither richer field context nor larger populations substantially close this gap. In blinded expert review, AI proposals trail the 2026 papers least in presentation and most in expected success, echoing their gap in concrete approaches, and those whose ideas no human paper shares fare worst, suggesting weaker directions rather than overlooked opportunities. These results indicate that the main bottleneck in AI research taste lies less in finding the directions a community works on than in turning them into the concrete approaches it goes on to pursue. We release IdeaTaste as an open, continuously updated leaderboard (https://cxcscmu.github.io/IdeaTaste) that benchmarks contemporary AI proposals against future publication cycles.
blocks.zh: 研究口味,对阅读内容的判断,追求哪些问题,尝试哪些方法,日益塑造了AI科学家的作品,然而它仍然远不如他们执行研究的能力. 我们引入了Idea Taste, 这个基准通过它从2025年被冻结的文献快照中写出的研究提案, 对一个LLM进行评分, 与2026年出版的同一批作品相匹配。 我们的实验跨越六个当代语言模型和四个研究领域,从既定领域到新兴领域,共涵盖90{}000多条建议。 LLM代理商在他们所引用的文献和所陈述的理念中都远远低于人类群体,在引用比对上达到了人类层面的26分左右,在思想比对上只有18分左右. 他们的人民可以像一个社区那样多样地引用并承担它的任务和方法,但很少达成它所追求的具体办法和研究计划。 既无较丰富的实地环境,也无较大人口大量弥合这一差距。 在盲目的专家审查中,大赦国际的建议在介绍2026份文件时最少,在预期中最成功,反映了它们在具体做法上的差距,而那些其思想没有人类论文的人的票价最高,表明方向较弱,而不是忽视机会。 这些结果表明,AI研究的主要瓶颈在于找到一个社区的工作方向,而不是把它们变成它所追求的具体方法。 我们公布Idea Taste作为公开的,不断更新的领跑板(https://cxcscmu.github.io/Idea Taste),该板将当代AI的建议与未来的出版周期比作基准.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: AI scientists can now carry out much of the research process on their own, from generating ideas and grounding them in prior work to running experiments and writing papers ( Lu et al., 2024 ; Yamada et al., 2025 ; Lu et al., 2026 ; Baek et al., 2025 ) . Frontier laboratories are deploying them at growing scale ( OpenAI, 2026 ; Anthropic, 2026 ; Gottweis et al., 2026 ; Chen et al., 2026a ) , and their work has begun to enter the scientific literature ( Tang et al., 2026 ; Bianchi et al., 2026 ) . Yet executing research well matters only when the research itself is worth doing, and this choice rests on research taste, the judgment of what to read, which problems to pursue, and which methods to try. As AI scientists take on a larger role in discovery, their taste increasingly shapes the research that comes next, but it remains far less understood than their ability to execute.
blocks.zh: AI科学家现在可以自行开展大部分研究过程,从产生想法并把它们扎入前期工作,到进行实验和撰写论文(Lu等,2024;Yamada等,2025;Lu等,2026;Baek等,2025.). 边疆实验室部署规模越来越大(OpenAI, 2026;Anthropic, 2026;Gottweis等, 2026;Chen等, 2026a),其工作开始进入科学文献(Tang等, 2026; Bianchi等, 2026.). 然而,只有在研究本身值得做的时候,才能很好地进行研究,而这种选择取决于研究的口味、对阅读内容的判断、所要追求的问题和尝试的方法。 由于AI科学家在发现中扮演了更大的角色,他们的口味日益塑造了接下来的研究,但是它仍然远不如他们的执行能力.

blocks.en: Evaluating research taste is challenging because it requires a reference for which choices are worth making. Existing work mostly judges one idea at a time, through expert ratings ( Si et al., 2025 ; Si et al., 2026 ) , benchmarks with fixed targets ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Qiu et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2025 ) , or model judges that predict which directions will matter ( Tian et al., 2026 ; Wu et al., 2026 ; Tong et al., 2026 ) , and such judgments are not yet reliable ( Sinhahajari et al., 2026 ; Ho et al., 2026 ; Baig et al., 2026 ) . Population-level studies find that generated ideas are highly similar within and across models ( Jiang et al., 2025 ; Wenger and Kenett, 2025 ; Chen et al., 2026b ) , but they measure how much a population repeats itself rather than whether its choices resemble those of human researchers. What is still missing is a direct comparison between the research choices of AI scientists and those of the human community working in the same area.
blocks.zh: 评价研究的口味具有挑战性,因为它需要一种值得选择的参考。 现有工作主要通过专家评分(Si等,2025;Si等,2026),判断一个有固定目标的基准(Guo等,2025;Quu等,2025;Chen等,2025;或预测哪个方向要紧的模型法官(Tian等,2026;Wu等,2026;Tong等,2026;),这种判断尚不可靠(Sinhahajari等,2026;Ho等,2026;Baig等,2026). 人口层面的研究发现,产生的想法在模型内部和模型之间高度相似(Jiang等人,2025年;Wenger和Kenett,2025年;Chen等人,2026年b),但它们衡量人口重复的次数,而不是其选择是否类似于人类研究人员的选择。 仍然缺少的是AI科学家的研究选择与在同一领域工作的人类社会的研究选择之间的直接比较.

blocks.en: Figure 1: Overview of IdeaTaste. The literature corpus is frozen through 2025. In the upper branch, the human research community goes on to publish 2026 papers that cite work in the corpus. In the lower branch, a population of LLM agents retrieves from the corpus and writes research proposals. Matching compares the two branches, and diversity compares proposals with one another.
blocks.zh: 图1:意向品概论. 文献资料库被冻结到2025年。 在上行分行,人类研究界继续发表2026篇论文,引用了本作中的工作. 在下层分支,LLM代理的人群从诉讼文书中取出并撰写研究提案. 匹配比较两个分支,多样性比较各提案.

blocks.en: The work a community goes on to publish provides such a reference, since it records which of the many possible directions its researchers actually chose. Published papers have already been used to score single ideas by their later impact and to reconstruct a held-out paper from its bibliography ( Jiang, 2026 ; Chen et al., 2026c ) . We extend this reference from single papers to entire communities and introduce IdeaTaste, a benchmark that scores an LLM by how closely the population of proposals it writes matches a research community. As shown in Fig. 1 , IdeaTaste freezes the literature of a research area through 2025, lets LLM agents, standing in for the ideation stage of AI scientists, write research proposals from this snapshot, and compares them with the papers the same community published in 2026. A proposal that no 2026 paper shares may still be a good direction the community has not yet taken, so we also test, through blinded expert review, whether such proposals are overlooked opportunities or weaker ideas.
blocks.zh: 一个社区继续出版的作品提供了这样一个参考,因为它记录了研究人员实际选择的许多可能方向中的哪一个。 出版的论文已经用来通过后期的影响来评分单一思想,并从其书目中重建了被搁置的论文(Jiang, 2026;Chen等, 2026c.). 我们把这一参考内容从单一文件推广到整个社区,并引入了Idea Taste这一基准,该基准通过它所撰写的提案数量与研究界的匹配程度来评分一个LLM。 如图一所示,"Idea Taste"冻结了一个研究区的文献直到2025年,让LLM代理,站在AI科学家的构思阶段,从这个快照中写出研究建议,并将其与2026年出版的同族论文相比较. 关于没有2026份纸质股份的建议可能仍然是社区尚未采取的良好方向,因此,我们也通过盲目的专家审查来检验这些建议是否被忽视的机会或弱小的想法。

blocks.en: Since new research both builds on prior work and recombines it into new ideas ( Uzzi et al., 2013 ; Foster et al., 2015 ) , we compare proposals and papers at two levels. The literature they cite reflects what they read, and the ideas they state reflect which problems they pursue and which methods they propose. At each level, matching measures agreement with the human papers and diversity measures how varied the proposals are, and both are read against the level the 2026 papers reach among themselves. The benchmark covers four areas ranging from established to emerging fields, namely machine learning systems, code generation, world models, and automated research. Four methods differ in what an LLM agent knows about its area, from nothing beyond the corpus to a single topic ( Lu et al., 2024 ) , a map of the whole area, and the proposals its population wrote in earlier rounds ( Schmidgall and Moor, 2025 ) . We benchmark six recent language models under each method, two of which were trained before 2026 and thus cannot have seen any reference paper.
blocks.zh: 由于新的研究既以先前的工作为基础,又将其重新整合为新的想法(Uzzi等,2013年;Foster等,2015年),因此我们在两个层面对提案和论文进行比较。 他们所引用的文献反映了他们所读到的,他们所说的思想反映了他们所追求的问题和他们提出的方法. 在每个级别,措施与人文论文一致,多样性衡量方法如何不同,两者都与2026年论文之间达到的水平相对照。 基准涵盖四个领域,从既定领域到新兴领域,即机器学习系统、代码生成、世界模型和自动化研究。 在LLM代理对其区域的了解方面,有四种方法不同,从除了本体之外没有其他方法,到一个单一的主题(Lu等人,2024年),一个整个地区的地图,以及它的人口在前几轮(Schmidgall and Moor,2025年)中提出的建议。 我们以每种方法为基准衡量最近六种语文模式,其中两种模式在2026年之前就已培训过,因此,无法看到任何参考文件。

blocks.en: Across more than 90,000 proposals, LLM agents fall well short of the research taste of human communities. Citation matching reaches about 26% of the human level on average and idea matching only 18%, and no population reaches half of it on either metric. The shortfall lies in what LLM agents propose more than in what they read. Given a direction, their populations can cite as diversely as a community and take up its tasks and methods, yet their proposals meet human papers far more often on problems and motivations than on concrete approaches and research plans. The gap also resists simple remedies. Models trained before 2026 match more human ideas than later ones that may have seen the reference, richer field context changes how widely a population spreads far more than how closely it follows human research, and populations up to 17 times larger level off well below the human level. In blinded expert review, AI proposals trail the 2026 papers least in presentation and most in expected success, echoing their gap in concrete approaches, and those whose ideas no human paper shares fare worst, suggesting weaker directions rather than overlooked opportunities. The main bottleneck in AI research taste thus lies less in finding the directions a community works on than in turning them into the concrete approaches it goes on to pursue. We release IdeaTaste as an open, continuously updated leaderboard that scores proposals written today against the research communities publish next. Our main contributions are as follows.
blocks.zh: 在9万多条建议中,LLM代理商远远没有达到人类社区的研究口味. 引用比对平均达到人类水平的约26%,想法只达到18%,没有人口达到一半。 缺点在于LLM代理商提出的建议比他们所读的要多。 鉴于一个方向,他们的人口可以像社区那样多样地引用并承担其各项任务和方法,然而,他们的建议更经常地与关于问题和动机的人类文件相会,而不是具体的方法和研究计划。 这种差距也抵制简单的补救办法。 2026年之前培训的模型比后来可能看到参考文献的模型更符合人类思想,更丰富的实地环境改变了人口分布的广度,远远超出其跟踪人类研究的程度,人口比人类水平低出17倍。 在盲目的专家审查中,大赦国际的建议在介绍2026份文件时最少,在预期中最有成功,反映了它们在具体做法上的差距,而那些没有人类论文的想法却与众不同,表明方向较弱,而不是忽视机会。 因此,AI研究的主要瓶颈在于找到一个社区的工作方向,而不是把它们变成它所追求的具体方法。 我们发布了Idea Taste,作为一个开放的,不断更新的领导板,评分今天写的建议反对研究团体接下来发表. 我们的主要贡献如下。

blocks.en: • We introduce IdeaTaste, a benchmark that evaluates the research taste of LLM agents against the papers human communities publish after a frozen literature snapshot, scoring matching and diversity on cited literature and stated ideas across four research areas. • Through experiments with six language models and four methods, covering more than 90,000 proposals, we find that LLM agents reach only a small fraction of the human level, lag more on ideas than on citations, and gain little from possible exposure to the reference, richer context, or larger populations. • Through direction coverage, slot-level decomposition, and blinded expert review, we show that LLM agents reach the directions a community pursues far more readily than the approaches it proposes, and that proposals missing the human record are weaker rather than merely different.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 我们提出Idea Taste这一基准,用来对照人类社区在被冻结的文献快照之后发表的论文,评估LLM代理的研究口味,对所引用的文献和四个研究领域的既定思想进行比对和多样性的评分。 · 通过6个语言模型和4个方法的实验,涉及90 000多条建议,我们发现LLM代理人只达到人类水平的一小部分,在思想上落后于引用,从可能接触参考物、较丰富的背景或更大的人群中得益甚微。 二. 支助 通过方向覆盖、时间档分解和盲目专家审查,我们表明,LLM代理人比它提出的办法更容易到达一个社区所追求的方向,而缺失人类记录的建议则较弱,而不仅仅是不同。

blocks.en: We introduce IdeaTaste, a benchmark that evaluates the research taste of LLM agents against the papers human communities publish after a frozen literature snapshot, scoring matching and diversity on cited literature and stated ideas across four research areas.
blocks.zh: 我们提出Idea Taste这一基准,用来对照人类社区在被冻结的文献快照之后发表的论文,评价LLM代理的研究口味,对所引用的文献和四个研究领域的既定思想进行评分和多样性。

blocks.en: Through experiments with six language models and four methods, covering more than 90,000 proposals, we find that LLM agents reach only a small fraction of the human level, lag more on ideas than on citations, and gain little from possible exposure to the reference, richer context, or larger populations.

blocks.en: Through direction coverage, slot-level decomposition, and blinded expert review, we show that LLM agents reach the directions a community pursues far more readily than the approaches it proposes, and that proposals missing the human record are weaker rather than merely different.
blocks.zh: 通过方向覆盖、时间档分解和盲目专家审查,我们显示,LLM代理人比它提出的办法更能容易地到达一个社区所追求的方向,而没有人类记录的建议则较弱,而不仅仅是不同。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: AI scientists are now built to run much of the research loop, from idea to experiment to written paper ( Lu et al., 2024 ; Yamada et al., 2025 ; Lu et al., 2026 ) , and the space is growing quickly ( Luo et al., 2025 ; Wei et al., 2025 ) . Agent Laboratory executes a human-provided idea, Co-Scientist refines hypotheses through a team of agents ( Schmidgall et al., 2025 ; Gottweis et al., 2026 ) , SciAgents and the Virtual Lab carry multi-agent designs into materials and biomedical problems ( Ghafarollahi and Buehler, 2025 ; Swanson et al., 2025 ) , and CycleResearcher adds automated review ( Weng et al., 2025 ) . Evaluation has largely followed one unit, a single system, even as agent-written work begins to enter the record from deployments at scale and a conference with AI authors and reviewers ( Tang et al., 2026 ; Bianchi et al., 2026 ; Zhong et al., 2026b ) . This paper moves up a level, to a population of LLM agents proposing research from one shared literature.
blocks.zh: AI科学家现被构建为运行从思想到实验到书面论文的许多研究循环(Lu等,2024;Yamada等,2025;Lu等,2026),空间正在迅速增长(Luo等,2025;Wei等,2025). Agent Laborator执行一个人提供的想法,共同科学家通过一组物剂(Schmidgall等人,2025年;Gottweis等人,2026年),SciAgents和虚拟实验室携带多剂设计,用于材料和生物医学问题(Ghafarollahi和Buehler,2025年;Swanson等人,2025年),循环研究员增加自动审查(Weng等人,2025年)。 评估主要遵循一个单位,一个系统,即使代理写作工作开始从规模部署中录入记录,并与AI作者和审查员开会(Tang等,2026;Bianchi等,2026;Zhong等,2026b.). 本文向上发展到一个水平, 成为LLM代理 提出研究 从一个共享的文献。

blocks.en: Within such systems the proposal comes from an ideation step, where methods turn retrieved prior work into problems, hypotheses, and experiment designs ( Baek et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2025 ; Hu et al., 2025 ) , and related work forecasts active topics from a knowledge graph ( Krenn et al., 2023 ; Gu and Krenn, 2025 ) . Ideation has also been run at population scale, on a shared archive or inside a simulated research community ( Schmidgall and Moor, 2025 ; Yu et al., 2024 ) , where outputs turn out to be substantially similar within and across models ( Jiang et al., 2025 ; Wenger and Kenett, 2025 ) , with further work relating this to knowledge, group size, and crowding against human output ( Deng et al., 2026 ; Chen et al., 2026b ; Azad and Baten, 2026 ) , as agent societies outside research also develop shared conventions and collective bias ( Park et al., 2023 ; Ashery et al., 2025 ) and agent ecosystems concentrate into homogeneous offerings ( Ling et al., 2026 ) . Such comparisons are mostly internal to the population. This study measures that similarity in the literature a proposal cites and in the idea it states, and pairs each with agreement against human papers.
blocks.zh: 在这类系统中,建议来自一个想法步骤,即方法将以前的工作转变为问题、假设和实验设计(Baek等人,2025年;Wang等人,2024年;Li等人,2025年;Hu等人,2025年),以及相关工作从知识图(Krenn等人,2023年;Gu和Krenn,2025年)中预测活跃专题。 此外,还在人口规模、共享档案或模拟研究社区内部进行了思想研究(Schmidgall and Moor,2025;Yu等人,2024;),其产出在模型内部和模型之间基本相似(Jiang等人,2025;Wenger and Kenett,2025;),其进一步工作涉及知识、群体规模和挤占人类产出(Deng等人,2026;Chen等人,2026b;Azad and Baten,2026;),作为外部研究的代理社会,还制定了共同公约和集体偏见(Park等人,2023;Ashery等人,2025;Ashery等人,2025;Ashery和Kenett,20),并将代理生态系统集中于同质供货(Ling等人,2026)。 这种比较主要是内部的。 这项研究衡量了一项提案在文献中所引述的和它所表述的理念中的相似性,并且将每项提案与人类论文相提并论。

blocks.en: Evaluation supplies the external reference such comparisons lack. Experts judge one idea at a time, though the initial advantage of model ideas narrowed once executed ( Si et al., 2025 ; Si et al., 2026 ) , while benchmarks score ideas against fixed targets ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Qiu et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2025 ) , often leaving the verdict to model judges ( Zheng et al., 2023 ; Huang et al., 2025b ) , now asked which directions will matter ( Tian et al., 2026 ; Wu et al., 2026 ; Tong et al., 2026 ) . Those verdicts are not yet reliable, as judges disagree with experts on novelty ( Sinhahajari et al., 2026 ) , trail them at comparison ( Baig et al., 2026 ) , and rate unsound ideas as sound ( Ho et al., 2026 ) , while human review is itself inconsistent ( Cortes and Lawrence, 2021 ) . Published research offers a steadier reference, used to score ideas by future impact ( Jiang, 2026 ) , to recover a held-out paper ( Chen et al., 2026c ) , and to profile ideas against a taxonomy on which model output is narrower ( Chen et al., 2026d ) , though citation lists are an imperfect standard ( Sahu et al., 2026 ) . This paper extends that reference from single papers to what a research community published after its literature was frozen, comparing that with what a population cites and proposes.
blocks.zh: 评价提供了这种比较缺乏的外部参考。 专家每次判断一个想法,虽然模型思想的初始优势一度被收缩(Si等,2025;Si等,2026),而基准对固定目标的评分(Guo等,2025;Quu等,2025;Chen等,2025),往往将判决留给模型法官(Zheng等,2023;Huang等,2025b),现在问到哪个方向很重要(Tian等,2026;Wu等,2026;Tong等,2026). 这些判决尚不可靠,因为法官与新颖性(Sinhahajari等,2026年)专家意见不一,比较后追踪(Baig等,2026年),将不正确的观念评为有理(Ho等,2026年),而人文审查本身则不一致(Cortes和Lawrence,2021年). 所发表的研究提供了更稳定的参考,用于通过未来影响来评分想法(江,2026),取回被搁置的论文(Chen等,2026c),并针对模型输出更窄的分类学(Chen等,2026d)来剖析想法,虽然引用列表是一个不完善的标准(Sahu等,2026). 本文将这一提法从单篇论文延伸至研究界在其文献被冻结后发表的内容,与人们引用和提议的内容作一比较。

blocks.en: 3 IdeaTaste
blocks.zh: 3 个想法

blocks.en: IdeaTaste evaluates the research taste of LLM agents by comparing the proposals they write from a frozen literature with the papers a human community later publishes. Sec. 3.1 builds the literature corpus and the human reference, Sec. 3.2 defines four metrics on what each side cites and proposes, and Sec. 3.3 describes the methods.
blocks.zh: Idea Taste通过比较他们从被冻结的文献中写出的建议和人类社会后来所发表的论文来评价LLM代理的研究口味. 第3.1条构建了文献和人类参考,第3.2条界定了每一方引用和提议的四分法,第3.3条描述了方法。

blocks.en: 3.1 Data Construction
blocks.zh: 3.1 国家 数据构建

blocks.en: We cover four research areas: machine learning systems and code generation, established fields with large literatures, and world models and automated research, smaller fields that are still emerging. For each area, we split the literature at the end of 2025. Papers published through 2025 form the corpus U U , which LLM agents search and propose from. Papers published in 2026 form the human reference H H , which records what the community actually pursued after this cutoff. The cutoff can be moved forward as new papers appear.

blocks.en: 3.2 Evaluation Design

blocks.en: Writing a research document, whether a human paper or an LLM agent proposal, involves two choices, selecting the prior work to build on and formulating an idea in relation to it. LLM agents make these choices using only the frozen corpus U U , while the human reference H H records the community’s subsequent choices after the cutoff. We therefore compare H H with the proposals A A of a population at the two corresponding levels ( Uzzi et al., 2013 ; Foster et al., 2015 ) . The resulting information asymmetry across the cutoff is discussed in Appendix E.4 . At the citation level, each document d ∈ H ∪ A d\in H\cup A is represented by its citation set 𝒞 ⁡ ( d ) \mathcal{C}(d) , the papers it cites that lie in U U . At the idea level, it is represented by a summary that a language model extracts from its abstract under a fixed schema of five slots ℐ \mathcal{I} , namely contribution type, problem, motivation, proposed approach, and research plan, as detailed in Appendix B . At each level, matching measures agreement with the human reference and diversity measures how varied the proposals are, giving citation matching Match-Cite , citation diversity Diversity-Cite , idea matching Match-Idea , and idea diversity Diversity-Idea . All four lie in [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] , and higher values mean closer agreement with the human reference or greater variety. Applying them to H H itself, with each human paper compared only with the other human papers, gives the human level against which populations are read.

blocks.en: 3.3 Methods
blocks.zh: 3.3 国家 方法

blocks.en: All four methods share one LLM agent implementation and differ only in what it knows about its area. The LLM agent receives the area definition used to screen the human reference and writes one proposal within a fixed step budget, taking one action per step: planning, searching the corpus, pinning retrieved papers, revising the draft, compressing its history into notes, or submitting. It can cite only retrieved papers, so its citations always lie in U U . The methods vary its profile and actions: • free only states that the LLM agent is a researcher in the area, revealing what it pursues without an explicit prior. • topic assigns one research topic and leaves the choice of problem open ( Lu et al., 2024 ) , testing how a broad direction shapes proposals. Topics are allocated in proportion to corpus frequency, with recent years upweighted. • landscape assigns no topic but lists the area’s most common task tags, method tags, and task–method pairs with their shares among 2025 papers, plus an action to retrieve papers by tag or pair. It thus exposes the area’s structure and how crowded each direction is, which researchers weigh when choosing between established and new directions ( Foster et al., 2015 ) . • frontier lets LLM agents see one another’s work ( Schmidgall and Moor, 2025 ) . It assigns topics like topic but runs in rounds, freezing each round’s proposals and research traces into a snapshot that later rounds query through two extra actions, as researchers read peers’ work. Peer records are separate from literature retrieval, uncitable, and marked as not scientifically validated. These methods test whether an LLM agent’s view of its area changes the literature and ideas its population selects. See Appendix C for more details.

LLM代理收到用于筛选人类参考文献的区域定义,并在固定的步法预算内写出一个建议,每步采取一个动作:规划,搜索本体,将取回的相纸贴上,修改草案,压缩其历史,或提交. 它只能引用检索到的论文, 这些方法不同其特征和行动: • 自由只声明LLM代理人是该地区的研究者,在没有明确前科的情况下揭示其追求的东西. • 专题指定一个研究专题,并开放问题选择(Lu等,2024年),测试大方向如何形成提案。 主题按体积频率的比例分配,近年来的重量有所增加。 – 地平线没有指定话题,而是列出该地区最常见的任务标记,方法标记,以及任务-方法配对及其在2025年论文中的份额,再加上通过标记或配对取回文件的行动. 因此,它揭示了该地区的结构以及每个方向的拥挤程度,研究人员在选择既定方向和新方向时会权衡这些方向(Foster等,2015年)。 前沿让LLM代理商互相看一看(Schmidgall和Moor,2025年)。 研究者阅读同行们的作品时, 同行记录与文献检索是分开的,不易辨认,并被标记为未经科学验证. 这些方法检验LLM代理对其区域的看法是否改变其人口所选择的文献和思想. 见附录 详情请查C.

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4个实验

blocks.en: We run the four methods of Sec. 3.3 in every area with the six language models in Table 2 . Each LLM agent has a budget of 20 steps, and each population holds 300 proposals, which frontier writes in two rounds of 150. The six models form two groups by design. Four were released in 2026 and power current AI scientists, so their training data may overlap the human reference, but leaving them out would confine the benchmark to outdated models. The other two were trained before 2026 and cannot have seen any 2026 paper, so their results are free of leakage by construction. Comparing the two groups tests whether possible exposure to the reference helps LLM agents anticipate 2026 research. Appendix C gives implementation details.
blocks.zh: 我们使用表2中的6个语言模型,在每个领域采用第3.3条的四种方法。 每一个LLM代理人的预算为20个步骤,每个人口持有300个提案,边境写作两轮150个. 这6个模型通过设计组成了两组. 4个在2026年发布,动力流的AI科学家,因此他们的训练数据可能与人类的参考数据相重叠,但将他们排除在外会将基准限制在过时的模型上. 另外两人在2026年之前就受过训练,无法见到任何2026年的论文,因此他们的结果没有被建筑渗出. 比较这两个组,测试是否可能接触参考物是否有助于LLM剂预测2026研究. 附 录 C提供实施的细节。

blocks.en: All populations are scored with the metrics of Sec. 3.2 , and scoring the 2026 papers against one another gives the human level. The slot-level judge is GPT-5.6 Luna, outside the evaluated model families and validated against human annotators in Appendix B.4 .
blocks.zh: 所有人口都得到3.2第(一)分的评分,对2026年论文的评分给予人的水平。 槽级法官是GPT-5.6 Luna,在被评价的模范家庭之外,并在附录B.4中针对人类的注释者进行验证。

blocks.en: Beyond whether LLM agents propose what the community pursues, we use human evaluation to examine how good their proposals are, and in particular whether those without a human counterpart are weak directions or sound ones the community has not yet taken. Eleven reviewers, all with reviewing experience, assess 192 documents without knowing their source. The documents are split evenly between proposals and 2026 papers and balanced across areas and models. Half come from matched pairs, each a proposal and the 2026 paper it overlaps under the judge of Match-Idea , and the other half have no counterpart on the other side. Each document receives two reviews. Besides the dimensions of a standard machine learning conference review form, reviewers rate feasibility and expected success, since an idea can look original yet fail in execution ( Si et al., 2026 ) , and guess whether the document is AI-generated. Appendix B.5 details the design.
blocks.zh: 除了LLM代理人是否提出社区所追求的目标之外,我们利用人的评价来考察他们的建议有多好,尤其是那些没有人类对应者的建议是弱方向还是社区尚未采取的好方向。 11名审查员都具有审查经验,在不知道文件来源的情况下评估了192份文件。 文件在提案和2026份文件之间分布均匀,在领域和模式之间平衡. 一半来自相配对,每个提案和2026年的论文在Match-Idea的评委下相重叠,而另一半则在另一边没有对应的. 每份文件都接受两次审查。 除了标准机器学习会议审查表的维度,审查者评定可行性和预期成功,因为一个想法看起来是原始的,但在执行中却失败了(Si等,2026),并猜猜该文件是否是AI生成的. 附录B.5详细介绍了设计.

blocks.en: Table 2 scores every population on the four metrics against the human level, and Table 3 reports how reviewers rate a blinded sample of proposals and 2026 papers. Together they yield four findings. • LLM agents fall far short of the research taste of human communities. On average, LLM agents reach about 26% of the human level on Match-Cite and only 18% on Match-Idea , and no population, under any model or in any area, reaches half of it on either metric. The gap is narrowest in automated research, the newest and smallest area, and widens as the area grows, peaking in machine learning systems and code generation. LLM agents thus track a community most closely where it has least to choose from and fall furthest behind where it has most. • The gap lies in what LLM agents propose, not in what they read. For five of the six models, matching falls further behind the human level on ideas than on citations, and diversity sharpens this split. Once topic or frontier assigns a direction, four of the six models cite up to three times as diversely as the community, yet no population reaches the human level of idea diversity. A population can thus read as widely as a community and still repeat itself in what it proposes, so drawing on the literature a community builds on is not enough to arrive at the ideas it pursues. • Knowing more, from training or from context, does not close the gap. Although four of the six models may have seen the 2026 papers in training, the two trained before 2026 match more human ideas, about 26% of the human level against 14% as Appendix E.4 details. Idea matching thus follows neither recency nor capability, as Llama 4 Scout matches the most human ideas yet receives the lowest ratings in Table 3 . More context does no better. Across the four methods, matching stays within a narrow band while citation diversity varies about threefold, so what an LLM agent is told shapes how widely its population spreads far more than how closely it follows human research. The fullest view helps least, as landscape ranks last on Match-Cite in 19 of 24 settings, while the direction of topic and the peer proposals of frontier broaden a population without bringing it near the human level. • The quality gap centers on execution and deepens where proposals miss the human record. In blind review, AI proposals score below the 2026 papers on every quality dimension, by 20 points on expected success but only 4 on presentation, so the gap lies less in how the proposals are written than in whether they would work. Reviewers also flag 86% of them as AI-generated, against 39% of the papers. Even DeepSeek-V4-Flash, which surpasses the papers on soundness, presentation, and contribution, trails them in feasibility and expected success. Split by match, both groups of proposals trail the papers by the same 11 points in overall rating, but those with no human counterpart fall much further behind in execution, as the gap widens from 8 to 15 points in feasibility and from 15 to 26 in expected success. The proposals that miss the human record are thus the ones reviewers expect least to succeed.
blocks.zh: 表2根据四个衡量标准对每个人口进行比对,表3报告审查人员如何评分盲目的建议书样本和2026篇论文。 它们合起来得出了四项结论。 • LLM剂远远低于人类社区的研究口味。 平均来说,Match-Cite的LLM剂达到人类水平的约26%,Match-Idea上只有18%,在任何模型下或任何地区,任何人口都无法达到任何衡量标准的一半。 这一差距在自动化研究中最窄,是最新和最小的区域,随着区域扩大而扩大,在机器学习系统和代码生成中达到顶峰. 因此,LLM代理人最密切地跟踪一个社区,在那里,它最不需要选择最落后的地方。 差距在于LLM代理人的建议,而不是他们读的. 对于六个模式中的五个模式,比对比比比比对引文更落后于人的层面,多样性使这种分裂更加尖锐. 一旦主题或前沿指定了方向,六个模式中就有四个引用最多是社区多样性的三倍,但没有任何人口达到人的思想多样性水平。 因此,人们可以像一个社区那样广泛阅读,并且仍然重复它的建议,因此,依靠一个社区所依赖的文献不足以得出它所追求的思想。 • 从培训或背景上了解更多的情况,并不能弥合差距。 虽然6个模型中有4个可能在训练中看到了2026年的论文,但两个在2026年前被训练过的论文与更多的人的思想相匹配,大约26%的人与14%作为附录E.4的细节. 因此,思想匹配既不遵循惯性,也不遵循能力,因为Llama 4 Scout与大多数人类思想相匹配,但却在表3中获得最低的收视率。 更多背景也没有更好的。 在四种方法中,匹配停留在一个狭长的带子内,而引用的多样性则有三分之多,因此,人们告诉一个LLM代理人的特征是,其人口分布的广度远大于它跟踪人类研究的密切程度。 在24个环境中,有19个环境在Match-Cite上占了最后一位,而主题的方向和边界的同龄人建议则扩大了人口的范围,但没有使其接近人的水平。 质量差距以执行为中心,在提案错过人类记录的地方会更深。 在盲目审查中,AI建议在每个质量层面的评分低于2026个论文,在预期成功方面评分为20分,但在列报方面评分为4分,因此,差距在于建议如何写而不是建议是否有效。 评论家还标出其中86%为AI出品,而论文比例为39%. 甚至DeepSeek-V4-Flash,它超过了关于健全性、表述和贡献的论文,在可行性和预期成功方面跟踪它们。 按对等划分,两组提案在总体评分中以同样的11分跟随论文,但无人对应方的提案在执行中远远落后,差距从可行性的8分扩大到可行性的15分,从预期成功率的15分扩大到26分。 因此,错失人类记录的建议是最不期望成功的建议。

blocks.en: We provide interesting cases with expert review as shown in Figure 2 . Case 1 shows that the proposal scored higher on soundness and on expected success. Case 2 collects three documents that no counterpart matched. The first is a 2026 paper rated below both and also taken for AI. The first proposal reads well enough for a middling overall rating, yet its feasibility and expected success sit near the bottom of the scale and the reviewer identified it as AI-generated. A reviewer took the second proposal for a published paper. Therefore, the averages in Table 3 place proposals below papers there, while individual documents on both sides span the range.
blocks.zh: 如图2所示,我们通过专家审查提供了有趣的案例。 案例1表明,提案在合理性和预期成功方面得分较高。 案件2收集了三份没有对应文件匹配的文件。 第一份是一份2026年的论文,评分为以下两个,也为AI所取. 第一项提案读取了足够的内容,足以对总体评级进行干涉,但其可行性和预期成功率接近比额表底部,审查者将其确定为AI生成. 一位评论员接受了第二份关于发表论文的建议。 因此,表3中的平均数将提案置于文件之下,而双方的个别文件则横跨范围。

blocks.en: 5 Analysis
blocks.zh: 5 分析

blocks.en: The main results show that LLM agents fall furthest behind on idea matching. We trace where this gap lies, first across research directions, then within the idea summary and in concrete cases, and finally ask whether larger populations close it.
blocks.zh: 主要结果显示LLM剂在思想相配方面落在最后方. 我们追踪这一差距的所在,首先跨越研究方向,然后在思想摘要和具体案例中,最后问人口是否增加。

blocks.en: Low idea matching may arise because a population never takes up the directions the 2026 papers pursue, or because it takes them up and still arrives at different ideas. To tell these apart, we treat a direction as a task paired with a method, that is, what a paper works on and how, and label both sides with the task and method vocabulary that landscape draws on. We run this comparison for DeepSeek-V4-Flash in automated research, with each population holding as many proposals as the area has papers so that both sides are compared at equal size. Figure 3 reports the share of human tag mass each population reaches. On each axis alone, the populations given a direction come close to the community, and frontier misses only a small share of the human task mass and of the method mass. On pairs, every population falls away, and even frontier reaches only about half of the human mass, so LLM agents work on the community’s tasks with its methods but combine the two differently. Neither kind of coverage, however, carries over to ideas. Frontier reaches about twice the human pair mass of free but matches barely more human ideas in Table 2 , where the four methods sit within a narrow band. LLM agents thus reach the directions a community pursues and still propose something else, so what they miss lies inside a direction rather than in the choice of one.
blocks.zh: 低思想匹配可能会出现,因为人们从不走2026年论文追求的方向,或者因为它带回了它们,仍然得出不同的想法. 把这些区分开来,我们把方向当作一个任务 与一种方法结合, 即,一个文件的工作原理和方式, 并标注两边的任务和方法词汇, 以图景借鉴。 我们对DeepSeek-V4-Flash进行这种比较,在自动化研究中,每个人群都持有和该地区有文件一样多的提案,这样双方的比较大小相同. 图3报告了每个人口所达到的人类标记质量的比例。 仅在每个轴线上,给定方向的人口就接近社区,而边疆只少了一小部分人类任务量和方法量. 在一对人中,每个人口都会下降,甚至边境也只达到人类总量的一半左右,因此LLM代理在社区的任务上用方法工作,但两者的结合方式不同. 然而,这两种报道都不随想法而去。 边疆达到人类免费质量的两倍, 因此,LLM代理人到达一个社区追求的方向,仍然提出其他建议,所以他们错过的就在于一个方向,而不是选择一个方向。

blocks.en: Figure 3: Tag use in automated research: the task a document works on, the method it uses, and the task–method pair. Left: how many distinct tags of each kind each population uses. Right: the cumulative share of human tag mass each population reaches, with human tags ordered from the most to the least used and the human curve as the ceiling.
blocks.zh: 图3:自动研究中使用的标记:文档使用的任务、使用的方法和任务-方法对等。 左:每类人口使用多少个不同的标记. 右:每个种群所达到的人类标记质量的累积份额,人类标记的订购量从最到最少使用,人类曲线为天花板.

blocks.en: To locate the difference inside an idea, we decompose Match-Idea into the slots of the idea summary. Table 4 reports per-slot matching for Llama 4 Scout and DeepSeek-V4-Flash, one model from each side of the 2026 cutoff. Both populations reach the problems and motivations of human papers many times more often than their approaches and research plans, so LLM agents agree with a community on what to study and why far more readily than on how to do it. Part of this ordering is intrinsic, since the 2026 papers also match one another far more often on problems than on approaches, an approach being the more specific of the two. Read against this human level, the decline persists for DeepSeek-V4-Flash, which covers a small share of human problems and almost none of their research plans, while Llama 4 Scout stays at roughly a third of the human level on every slot. Either way, almost no human approach or research plan finds a counterpart among the proposals, and this is where the idea gap lies.
blocks.zh: 为了找到一个想法内部的区别,我们把Match-Idea分解成想法摘要的插槽. 表4汇报了Llama 4 Scout和DeepSeek-V4-Flash的每秒比对情况,2026年截取赛中各有一个模式. 这两种人接触人类论文的问题和动机的次数比他们的方法和研究计划要多很多倍,因此,LLM代理商同意一个社区的意见,即研究什么,为什么比如何研究要容易得多。 这一命令的一部分是固有的,因为2026年的论文在问题上也比在方法上更经常地相互匹配,这种方法是两者中更为具体的。 与人类水平相对照的是,DeepSeek-V4-Flash的衰落持续了下来,它涵盖了人类问题的一小部分,几乎没有他们的研究计划,而Llama 4 Scout则停留在每个槽上大约为人类水平的三分之一. 无论哪种方式,几乎没有人的方法或研究计划在提案中找到对应的,这就是思想差距所在.

blocks.en: Table 4: Per-slot Match-Idea over the slots of the idea summary, namely problem, motivation, proposed approach, and research plan. Each entry is the share of human papers a population matches on that slot.

blocks.en: Figure 4 pairs each of two human papers with two proposals from one language model that share its problem. In both cases, the proposal that misses the human approach leaves the trained network unchanged and adds machinery around it, whereas the human paper and the matching proposal both modify the network itself. The Case 1 paper fine-tunes the router toward expert reuse, while proposal A predicts expert demand and prefetches experts around an unchanged network. The Case 2 paper updates low-rank adapters on a frozen network, while proposal A keeps the weights fixed and adapts through retrieved transitions. The same problem thus admits very different mechanisms, and a shared problem does not imply a shared approach. Appendix E.9 provides the source schemas and further examples.
blocks.zh: 图4是两篇人类论文的每篇配对,其中两个提案来自一个语言模型,共同提出问题. 在这两种情况下,不采用人的方法的建议使训练有素的网络保持不变并增加了周围的机械,而人文论文和匹配建议都修改了网络本身. 案例1的论文将路由器微调为专家再利用,而提案A则预测专家的需求和预济会专家围绕一个没有变化的网络进行. "案例2"论文在被冻结的网络上更新了低等适配器,而提案A则通过被检索到的过渡保持了权重的固定和适应. 因此,同样的问题承认了非常不同的机制,一个共同的问题并不意味着采取共同的办法。 附录E.9提供了来源计划和进一步的例子。

blocks.zh: 图4:两篇人文论文,每篇都与来自单一语言模式的两篇AI提案相配. 在储存的自动判断下,所有四项提案都与关于问题和动机的人类论文相匹配,只有提案B也与拟议的方法和研究计划相匹配.

blocks.en: If the gap stemmed mainly from population size, sampling more proposals should close it. We grow the free and topic populations of Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and DeepSeek-V4-Flash in every area from 300 proposals to the size of the human reference, 3.8 to 17 times larger, and report matching in Figure 5 . Matching grows far more slowly than the population. Every curve rises only gently and levels off as proposals accumulate, staying well below the human level even when a population holds as many proposals as the community holds papers. An assigned direction helps somewhat, as topic climbs more steeply on ideas than free in most settings, yet both remain far from the human level. The gap is thus not an artifact of population size. Together with the analyses above, this shows that neither reaching more of a community’s directions nor writing more proposals brings LLM agents closer to the approaches the community arrives at. Improving research taste therefore means improving how a recognized problem becomes a concrete approach, not how widely or how much a population proposes.
blocks.zh: 如果差距主要来自人口规模,则更多的抽样建议应能弥补差距。 我们把双子座3.5闪光灯和DeepSeek-V4闪光灯的免费和专题量从300个提案增加到人类参考物的3.8至17倍,并在图5中报告匹配情况。 匹配增长比人口慢得多。 每道曲线只会轻而易举地上升,随着提案的积累而变平,即使人口持有的议案与社区持有的论文一样多,也远远低于人的水平。 指定的方向有所帮助,因为大多数情况下,话题比自由更尖锐地关注思想,但两者都远未达到人的水平。 因此,这一差距不是人口规模的一环。 这与上述分析一起表明,既未达到社区更多的方向,也未写出更多的提案,使LLM代理人更接近社区所达到的方法。 因此,改善研究的口味意味着如何改进一个公认的问题成为一个具体的办法,而不是人口提议的范围或多少。

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: We introduced IdeaTaste, a benchmark that measures the research taste of LLM agents against the research human communities go on to publish. Our results point to a consistent picture. LLM agents share much of a community’s literature and directions, yet seldom arrive at the concrete approaches it pursues, and the proposals that depart from human research tend to be weaker rather than overlooked. This picture holds across newer models, richer context, and larger populations. The research taste of LLM agents is thus limited less by knowing what to work on than by deciding how to pursue it, which we see as the central challenge for future AI scientists.
blocks.zh: 我们引入了Idea Taste, 这个基准衡量LLM剂的研究口味 与研究人类社区继续发表。 我们的结果显示一个一致的情况。 LLM代理商分享一个社区的很多文献和方向,但很少达成它所追求的具体方法,而脱离人类研究的建议往往较弱而不是被忽视。 这一情况涉及较新的模型、较丰富的背景和更多的人口。 因此,LLM剂的研究口味受到的限制较少,因为知道应该做什么工作,而不是决定如何进行,我们认为这是未来AI科学家的中心挑战.

blocks.en: Each area is represented by two sets of papers: a corpus U U of work published through 2025, which is what LLM agents retrieve from, and a human reference H H of papers from 2026, which is what proposals are measured against. The two are built to different standards. The corpus has to be wide enough that the background a 2026 paper builds on lies inside it, and it must carry nothing from 2026. The reference set has to be as complete as we can make it and has to hold research in the area. This appendix describes the area definitions, the sources data come from, data construction details, and the survey reference coverage audit.
blocks.zh: 每个领域都有两套文件:2025年出版的U U工作本,即LLM代理从中取出的东西;2026年的论文人文参考H,即建议衡量对象. 两者按不同的标准构建. 书目必须足够宽广,以至于2026年的论文所基于的背景就在于其中,从2026年起,它必须没有任何内容. 该参考集必须尽我们所能地完成,并且必须进行这方面的研究。 本附录介绍地区定义,来源数据出处,数据构建细节,调查参考范围审计等情况.

blocks.zh: A.1 研究领域

blocks.en: Each area is defined in writing before collection begins, and that definition does not change afterwards. It states what belongs to the area and what does not, and it is what every screening step below applies. The LLM agents receive the same text as the description of their research community, so both sides work under one definition of the area. Table 5 gives the four definitions together with the topic search queries used to collect the reference set.
blocks.zh: 每个区域在收集开始前都是书面定义的,而该定义在收集开始后不会改变. 它说明了哪些属于该地区,哪些不属于该地区,下面的每个筛选步骤都适用。 LLM代理公司收到与其研究界描述相同的文本,因此双方都根据一个区域的定义工作. 表5列出了四项定义以及收集参考文献所用的专题查询。

blocks.en: A.2 Data Collection
blocks.zh: A.2 数据收集

blocks.en: Collection has to satisfy one requirement: the corpus must hold the earlier work a 2026 paper builds on. We therefore run a single expansion out of hand-picked landmark papers along citation edges, and a paper’s publication year decides which set it joins, the corpus through 2025 and the reference set in 2026. The reference set carries a second requirement, since it is the record every metric is read against. Research the community did that we fail to collect is invisible to the scores, and a proposal that reached it would count as reaching nothing, so the set has to be as complete as we can make it. We therefore reach it by topic search over the area as well as by citation, and screen what both paths return against the area definition.
blocks.zh: 收集工作必须满足一项要求:委托书必须保存一份2026年的文件。 因此,我们用手摘取的具有里程碑意义的论文沿着引用边缘进行一次扩展,一个论文出版年度决定了它加入的内容、到2025年的程序和2026年的参考。 参考数据集载有第二项要求,因为它是每个衡量标准对照的记录。 研究一下我们未能收集到的社群 对于得分来说是隐形的,一个达到它的建议会算不上是一无所获,所以这个集必须尽可能地完整. 因此,我们通过对该地区的专题搜索和引用来达到这个目标,并对照地区定义来筛选两种路径返回的内容。

blocks.en: Each area starts from 20 to 22 landmark papers chosen by hand, listed in Table 6 . The corpus then grows in two steps. Descendants are papers published through 2025 that cite at least one landmark paper. Ancestors are papers cited by at least two distinct descendants. The second step brings in shared background that may not use the area’s terminology, and the threshold of two is what keeps it from pulling in everything a descendant happens to cite. Nothing on this side is screened for the area, since the corpus is a pool to retrieve from and a paper outside the area costs little as long as the background is there.
blocks.zh: 每个地区开始于20至22份手取的里程碑式文件,列于表6。 尸体会分两步生长 后代是2025年出版的论文,其中至少引用了一篇具有里程碑意义的论文. 祖先是至少由两个不同的后人所引用的论文. 第二步带来了共同的背景,可能没有使用该地区的术语,而第二步的门槛是阻止它拉动任何后裔偶然引用的东西。 这一边没有任何人被检查到这个地区,因为这个尸体是用来取回这个地区的水池,只要有背景,这个地区外的纸就花费不多了。

blocks.en: • Collection paths. Papers published in 2026 that cite a landmark continue the citation expansion directly, but many of them only use a released model or system rather than doing research in the area. Topic search over the area reaches what that path misses, including work that cites no landmark at all, so we collect along both. • Screening. Both paths are screened against the area definition, one DeepSeek-V4-Flash call per paper in JSON mode with the prompt and the rule it applies given in Figure 6 . The model returns a decision, a confidence, and a one-sentence reason, and each paper is judged once. The reference set is the union of what survives. • Filtering. We then remove surveys, duplicate records, and records that also appear in the corpus (using title and author list to filtering), which happens when a preprint and its published version are indexed separately.

blocks.en: We collect one record per paper, carrying its title and abstract, its publication date, its reference list, and the papers that cite it. Records come from OpenAlex ( Priem et al., 2022 ) and Semantic Scholar ( Kinney et al., 2023 ) . Records from the two sources are merged by identifier (DOI, arXiv id, etc.). Each index leaves reference lists unparsed for part of the corpus, and the edges they do report overlap only in part, so we merge the two and treat the union as a paper’s reference list. Publication dates missing from both are recovered from the arXiv API for preprints and from Crossref otherwise. Abstracts that neither index carried were recovered from the Springer, Elsevier and IEEE metadata services, from the first page of open-access PDFs, and by hand from a publisher’s page. Reference lists for 2026 papers that no index had parsed were recovered from full text where an index held it and otherwise from the PDF itself. After this pass every paper in the reference set has an abstract and almost all carry reference lists that resolve into the corpus for their area, while in the corpus nearly all records have abstracts and about two thirds carry reference lists as shown in Table 9 .

blocks.en: A.3 Coverage of Survey References
blocks.zh: A.3 调查参考资料的覆盖面

blocks.en: References from authoritative surveys provide an external check on how much of an area’s literature the collection holds. The audit screens each survey’s references for the area and measures how many of them that area’s own collection holds, its corpus together with its reference set. A reference we collected under another area counts as missing, since an LLM agent working in this area never retrieves it. Table 10 lists the surveys behind the audit. The references are screened one at a time by a language model with the same prompt shown in Figure 6 , which decides from the title since a reference record carries no abstract.

References is the length of a survey’s reference list, read from Semantic Scholar, or parsed from the survey’s arXiv page for those that Semantic Scholar returns no references for. In area is what remains after screening those references for the area. The area rows count such a work once, which is why they are smaller than the sum of the surveys below them, and they match the References column of Table 11 .

blocks.en: Table 11 reports the result. For code generation the table also audits a corpus built by filtering OpenAlex ( Priem et al., 2022 ) for the code generation keyword instead of expanding along citations, which reaches only a small fraction of the same references. That gap is the argument for expanding along citations: much of what an area builds on does not call itself by the area’s name. Automated research has the lowest coverage of the four, and its audit is the one that reaches furthest into 2026. blocks.en: A.4 Interpretation of the Human Reference
blocks.zh: A.4 人类参考资料的解释

blocks.en: The reference we score against is the set of 2026 papers in each area. By 2026 some of these papers are written with model assistance, and many are preprints that no venue has reviewed, so the set is not peer-reviewed, purely human work. This does not weaken its role in the benchmark as a measure of human research activity. Every paper in the reference was released by its authors. Releasing a paper is a human decision: the authors judged the problem worth pursuing and the work worth putting on the record. That judgment is what we compare against, and it stands whether or not a model helped write the text and whether or not a venue has reviewed it. What we compare against is research taste, i.e., the problems and ideas the authors chose. Whether a 2026 paper is strong or weak therefore does not change the measurement, since a weak paper still marks a direction a human researcher chose to pursue. What the benchmark asks is whether an LLM agent population proposes the problems and ideas that human researchers pursued, that is, whether it can reach ideas at the human level.
blocks.zh: 我们得分的参考文献是每一地区的2026份论文集。 到2026年,这些论文中有一些是在模型协助下撰写的,很多是没有场地审查过的预印,因此该集没有同行评审,纯属人文作品. 这不会削弱其在衡量人类研究活动的基准中的作用。 参考文献中的每一篇论文都由作者发布. 发表一篇论文是人类的决定:作者判断问题值得追求,而作品值得记录在案. 这一判断是我们所比较的,它表明一个模型是否帮助撰写了案文,以及一个地点是否审查了案文。 我们比较的是研究品味,即作者选择的问题和想法. 因此,2026年的论文是强是弱并不改变测量,因为一纸软弱仍然标志着人类研究者选择追求的方向. 基准问题在于LLM代理人口是否提出了人类研究人员所追求的问题和想法,即能否在人类层面达到想法.

blocks.en: A.5 Interpretation of research taste.
blocks.zh: A.5 研究口味的解释。

blocks.en: IdeaTaste uses research taste in a descriptive sense. A research community faces many plausible problems and methods but chooses to pursue only a small subset. We therefore treat papers released after the cutoff as observations of these realized research choices. The human reference captures which prior work researchers build on, which problems they pursue, and which approaches they develop. It does not assume that every published paper is high quality or that publication defines scientific value. Accordingly, MATCH-CITE and MATCH-IDEA measure how closely an LLM agent population anticipates the subsequent choices of the corresponding human community. High matching does not by itself imply higher research quality, and low matching does not by itself imply lower quality. The benchmark measures agreement with realized community choices rather than a normative standard of scientific merit. The blinded expert study helps interpret the gap beyond matching alone. A non-matching proposal could represent a valuable direction that the human community did not pursue. However, non-matching AI proposals are judged less feasible and less likely to succeed than non-matching human papers. This suggests that the observed gap is not explained only by different research preferences. We therefore view IdeaTaste as measuring one operational aspect of research taste: whether LLM agents anticipate the research choices that a human community later makes.

blocks.en: A.6 Interpreting Corpus Size
blocks.zh: A.6 解释公司大小

blocks.en: Corpus ( ≤ 2025 \leq 2025 ) size follows from how the citation expansion runs rather than from how large an area is. Code generation ends with the largest corpus of the four and a smaller reference set than machine learning systems, and both follow from the same cause. Several code generation landmarks are cited across natural language processing, semantic parsing, and software engineering, so their descendants reach well beyond the area, while the machine learning systems landmarks are cited mostly inside the systems community. Ancestors are drawn from those descendants, so the difference compounds at the second step. For the reference set the same breadth works the other way, since screening for the area removes the general natural language processing papers that cite those landmarks. A corpus size therefore records how widely an area’s research is built on elsewhere, not how much work the area itself produces.

blocks.en: System You are a research schema extractor. Given a paper abstract, extract that paper’s idea schema as a single JSON object. FOUR RULES THAT OVERRIDE EVERYTHING BELOW R1. Faithfulness outranks the rubric. The field descriptions below describe what a well-posed research idea looks like; they are NOT a standard the paper must be edited to meet. Extract what this abstract actually says. Where the abstract falls short of a description --- an evaluation with no stated failure condition --- record it as it is and note the shortfall in quality_note. Never repair, sharpen, or complete the paper. An invented scope, baseline, metric, or failure condition is a far worse error than a thin field. R2. Missing means missing. If the abstract supplies nothing for a schema field, that field’s entire value is the string "None", and for a list field the single element ["None"]. Use that exact word --- not a sentence explaining what is missing, not JSON null, not an empty string --- and never back-fill the field from another one that does have content. Three exemptions: ‘contribution_type.primary‘ is always one of the listed types (it is your classification, not something the abstract has to supply); ‘contribution_type.secondary‘ is [] when there is no genuine second contribution; and the three quality_check fields follow their own instructions below. R3. A defective abstract does not lower the bar and does not raise it. If the text is truncated, a stub, or otherwise not a real abstract, extract whatever it genuinely supports and set every other field to "None" --- do not compensate by inferring from the title, the venue, or what such papers usually do. Report the defect through abstract_complete and quality_note. The schema of a defective abstract is expected to be mostly not-stated; that is the correct output, not a failure. R4. Two bans apply to every field. (a) Anonymity. Do NOT copy any name this paper coins for its own contribution --- not the system, tool, framework, benchmark or dataset it proposes, and equally not a metric, principle, concept or phenomenon it names, in full form or as an acronym. ’We propose FooBar’ becomes ’the proposed framework’; ’introducing Near-Free Parallelism (NFP), the maximum number of positions executable at near-free latency’ becomes ’the maximum number of positions executable at near-free latency’, with every later NFP replaced the same way; ’we introduce PASS@(k,T), a two-dimensional metric’ becomes ’a two-dimensional metric’. A coined name is identifying even when it reads like ordinary technical vocabulary --- if the abstract is the thing that introduces the term, describe the concept instead of naming it. Also no title and no author names. Names of PRIOR work, baselines, and third-party models, datasets and libraries are NOT covered by this ban: keep them wherever the abstract gives them. (b) No outcomes. Do NOT copy results or performance numbers (accuracies, speedups, improvement ratios, win rates, acceptance counts) into any field: give the claims, the approach, and the evaluation design, not how they turned out. Quantities that define the setting rather than report a result --- model scale, token budget, dataset size, number of released tasks --- are allowed, and belong in a claim’s scope or in the approach. OUTPUT English only, whatever the abstract’s language. Budgets, which are caps and not targets: problem, motivation --- 1-2 sentences each. proposed_approach --- 2-4 sentences. research_plan --- up to 6 sentences (it usually needs them; the others usually do not). quality_note --- 1 sentence. When a field’s content does not fit its budget, drop by this order rather than compressing everything into an unreadable list: in research_plan, keep which evidence bears on which claim, then the failure conditions and what is held matched, and drop the enumeration of every baseline and metric name first; in proposed_approach, keep the mechanism and drop release/scale detail first. Never drop a field to "None" to save room --- that value means the abstract said nothing, and using it for anything else corrupts the downstream not-stated statistics. SCHEMA FIELDS contribution_type --- The form of the contribution, exactly one of these five in ‘primary‘: theory --- establishes what is or is not possible, or gives a formalism: proofs, bounds, characterizations, and the framings and problem formulations they rest on. method --- a new or modified technique meant to do a task better or newly at all. empirical_analysis --- measures or explains behaviour of things that already exist; the contribution is the finding, not a technique. artifact --- a dataset, benchmark, system, library, or model release; the contribution is the thing itself and its fitness for use. position --- argues that the field should frame, evaluate, or prioritize something differently; the contribution is the argument. Put another type in ‘secondary‘ only if the work genuinely delivers it too, else []. This is a contribution axis, not a domain --- a paper applying diffusion models to protein design is still ‘method‘. Classify by which kind of evidence the work must bring, not by what it ships: a benchmark paper whose point is what the benchmark reveals about existing models is ‘empirical_analysis‘ with ‘artifact‘ secondary. When the abstract is too thin to classify confidently, choose the closest type anyway and say in quality_note that the classification is uncertain. problem --- What is currently not known, not achievable, or not correctly formulated. Descriptive, and stated without naming the paper’s solution: someone who has not heard the idea should still recognize it as a gap. For ‘position‘ work the gap may be a defect in how the field frames or evaluates something rather than an open technical question. motivation --- Why this is worth solving now: what becomes possible, what cost is avoided, or what newly available capability makes it tractable. Do not restate the gap. proposed_approach --- What is built and how: method design, proof strategy, construction protocol, or system architecture, including what is released and at what scale. Execution only --- not the assertion, not the evidence it worked. research_plan --- The evidence the paper brings to bear on its claims, and what would count as support or as failure. Number the claims when they get different evidence (’(1) ... (2) ...’). Evidence means proofs and assumption-tightness arguments, experiments with named baselines and metrics, ablations isolating the component a claim credits, robustness checks, or quality audits; which of these counts depends on contribution_type (a ‘theory‘ paper’s evidence is its proof, an ‘artifact‘ paper’s is its quality audit and coverage analysis). Give a failure condition only where the abstract implies one, and say what is held matched (compute, parameters, latency) for trade-off claims when the abstract says. Describe the design, never the outcome. QUALITY CHECK --- about the abstract as a text, not about the paper. These three fields are exempt from R2: they always carry a real value. abstract_complete --- boolean. true if this is a real, untruncated abstract; false if it is a stub, a citation placeholder, a fragment, or otherwise not an abstract. abstract_sufficient --- boolean. true if it carries enough to fill the schema without guessing. quality_note --- one sentence naming which fields you left as "None", whether the contribution_type classification is uncertain, and where the abstract fell short of a field’s description. If none of those apply, the value is exactly "None". Respond with a single JSON object only. User Abstract: <abstract> Return JSON with exactly this shape: {"schema": {"contribution_type": {"primary": "method", "secondary": []}, "problem": "...", "motivation": "...", "proposed_approach": "...", "research_plan": "..."}, "quality_check": {"abstract_complete": true/false, "abstract_sufficient": true/false, "quality_note": "..."}} ‘primary‘ must be one of: theory, method, empirical_analysis, artifact, position --- never "None"; ‘secondary‘ is [] when there is no genuine second contribution. Any other schema field the abstract supplies nothing for is exactly "None".

blocks.en: The idea metrics rest on one decision, whether two summaries agree on a given slot. In this section, we sample pairs the judge has already ruled on and have people make the same decision without seeing its answer.
blocks.zh: 设想的衡量尺度取决于一个决定,即两个摘要是否就某一时间段达成一致。 在这个节中,我们抽样对对 法官已经做出裁定, 并让人们做出同样的决定 不看它的答案。

blocks.zh: 图 9:同想判断界面,显示一例. 左边的平面图给出了两个想法摘要;右边的平面图说明了法官得到的标准并收集了四个时档决定,全想决定,以及信心.

blocks.en: Figure 9 shows one example. The two left panes give the two idea summaries, the five slots contribution type, problem, motivation, proposed approach, and research plan, so an annotator decides on the same material the judge reads. The right pane carries the judge’s own instruction, narrowed to the four slots asked, and collects the answers in the two stages the judge works in. First, problem, motivation, proposed approach, and research plan are each marked same or different, judged as if the other slots were hidden, and a slot that one side leaves empty counts as different. Second, the annotator says whether the two documents describe the same core idea, and records a confidence from one to five.
blocks.zh: 图9举出一个例子。 两个"左派"给出了两个想法摘要,五个"槽"的贡献类型,问题,动机,提议的方法,以及研究计划,因此一个注释员决定了法官所读的同一份材料. 右面板带有法官自己的指示,缩小到所问的四个位置,并在法官工作的两个阶段收集答案。 首先,问题,动机,提议的方法,和研究计划,每个标记都相同或不同,判断时就好像其他的槽被隐藏了一样,一个槽,一方留下的空数算作不同. 第二,注释者说,这两份文件是否描述了同一个核心思想,并记录了从一到五的自信.

blocks.en: The study covers automated research and uses 40 judged summary pairs containing 160 slot pairs. Half are a proposal against a 2026 paper, taken from the Match-Idea judgments, and half are a proposal against another proposal of the same population, taken from the Diversity-Idea judgments. Sampling at random would leave little to compare, since the judge finds agreement on the whole idea in fewer than one in a thousand of the Match-Idea pairs it rules on, so nearly every drawn pair would be an easy disagreement. We instead stratify on what the judge decided: pair type crossed with its decisions on problem and motivation gives eight cells, and we draw five pairs from each. The sample then realizes 14 of the 16 possible combinations of the four decisions an annotator is asked to repeat, and is close to balanced on each of them as shown in Table 13 .
blocks.zh: 该研究涵盖自动化研究,并使用包含160个插槽对的40个判断分量的总结对. 一半是反对2026年论文的提案,取自Match-Idea判决;而一半是反对同一人口的另一个提案,取自多样性-Idea判决. 随机抽样将没有什么可比较的,因为法官在不到千分之一的Match-Idea配对中发现整个想法一致,所以几乎每对配对都很容易产生分歧. 相反,我们根据法官的决定来划分:一对类型与它对问题和动机的决定相交叉,有八个细胞,我们从每个细胞中划出五个对。 样本随后发现,在四种决定的16种可能组合中,有14种要求注释员重复,并且如表13所示,这些组合在每种组合上接近平衡。

blocks.en: Three annotators, a master’s student, a PhD student, and a PhD in computer science, each answer all 40 pairs, so every slot decision carries three independent human answers, which we reduce to a majority label. To gauge the judge’s stability, we run it five times on the same pairs. Table 13 reports, slot by slot, how often the judge marks a match, how far its runs agree, and how closely it agrees with the annotators’ majority. The five runs agree 77– 90 % 90\% of the time, so the verdict is largely reproducible. The judge also tracks the annotators’ majority closely on the problem and the proposed approach, while the more interpretive motivation and research-plan slots run lower. On most slots this alignment matches or exceeds the agreement among the annotators themselves, so the judge reads a pair about as consistently as a human would.
blocks.zh: 三位注释员,一位硕士生,一位博士生,以及一位计算机科学博士,每人都回答所有40对,所以每个插槽决定都包含三个独立的人类答案,我们把它简化为多数的标签。 为了衡量法官的稳定性,我们用同一对进行5次。 表13按档次排列的报告、法官的评分、评分一致的频率、评分一致的程度、评分一致的程度。 五行同意77 — 90% 90 — —%的时间,因此判决基本上可以复制。 法官还密切跟踪有关该问题和拟议办法的注释者多数,而解释性更强的动机和研究计划的时间档则较低。 在大多数位置上,这种校正与注释者本身的协议一致或超过协议,因此法官读出一对一致的,和人类一样.

The left pane presents the work as its title, abstract, and the structured summary of Sec. 3.2 , the five slots contribution type, problem, motivation, proposed approach, and research plan. The right pane collects the ratings: soundness, presentation, and contribution on the review form’s four-point scale, feasibility on a five-point scale from not at all to easily, expected success as one of five probability bands, an overall rating from strong reject to strong accept, a confidence from one to five, and a blinding check of real paper, AI-generated, or unclear.
blocks.zh: 图10举出一例。 左面框将作品作为标题,抽象,以及结构化的"Sec. 3.2"摘要,即五个档次的贡献类型,问题,动机,提议的方法和研究计划. 右面板收集评分:评分:评分表四分表的正确性、表述和贡献;五分表的可行性从不简单到容易;作为五个概率段之一的预期成功;从强烈拒绝到强烈接受的总体评分;从一到五的自信;以及真实纸张的盲目检查,AI生成,或不明确。

blocks.en: The questionnaire holds 192 research documents, split evenly between LLM agent proposals and 2026 papers so the blinding check cannot be won by favoring the more common label. Each area contributes 48 documents and each model 16 proposals, drawn from the free , topic , and landscape . The documents come in four kinds, shown in Table 14 : an AI proposal that overlaps a 2026 paper, the paper it overlaps, an AI proposal that overlaps no candidate paper, and a 2026 paper that no proposal overlaps. Overlap is decided by the slot-level judge of Match-Idea . Among the overlapping proposals, some match their paper on the whole idea and some only on the problem, and both are kept.
blocks.zh: 问卷持有192份研究文件,在LLM代理提案和2026份论文之间平分,因此通过偏好更常见的标签无法赢得盲文检查. 每个领域提供48份文件和16个模式提案,分别取自免费、专题和景观。 文件分为四类,如表14所示:AI提案与2026年的论文相重叠;它与论文相重叠;AI提案与没有候选论文相重叠;2026年的论文与提案相重叠. 重叠由Match-Idea的分档级法官决定。 在重叠的提案中,有些提案与他们关于整个想法的论文相符,有些提案只涉及问题,两者都保留下来。

blocks.en: The documents are split into six blocks of 32, each covering the four areas and a subset of the models. A proposal and the 2026 paper it overlaps are placed in different blocks, so no human reviewers see both and a paired comparison cannot turn into a within-reviewer ranking; the paired comparison is therefore made across reviewers, with a reviewer random effect in the analysis. Each reviewer takes one block one time and rates all 32 documents one time. One reviewer may take multiple blocks and record their background and experience as shown in Figure 11 . We only record reviewers who have review experience. We finally recruited 11 reviewers and collected two records for each block, that is, two review records for each research document.

blocks.en: As shown in Figure 10 , review design mainly follows the official review form of a major machine learning conference and scores an idea on seven dimensions. • Soundness, Presentation and Contribution use four levels (1 = poor, 2 = fair, 3 = good, 4 = excellent). • Feasibility uses five levels (1 = not at all, 5 = easily). • Expected success uses five probability bins ( < < 10%, 10–30%, 30–50%, 50–70%, > > 70%), coded 1–5. • Rating uses six levels (0 = strong reject, 2 = reject, 4 = marginally below, 6 = marginally above, 8 = accept, 10 = strong accept). • Confidence uses five levels (1 = unable to assess, 5 = absolutely certain). • Blinding check asks whether the reviewer thinks the entry is a real 2026 paper, an AI-generated proposal, or they cannot tell.
blocks.zh: 如图10所示,审查设计主要遵循主要机器学习会议的正式审查形式,并在七个维度上评出一个想法. • 健全、列报和贡献采用四个级别(1个=差,2个=公平,3个=好,4个=优)。 • 可行性采用5个级别(1个=根本没有,5个=容易)。 ● 预期成功使用5个概率箱( < 10%、10-30%、30-50%、50-70%、 > 70%),编码为1-5。 评级使用6个等级(0=强烈拒绝、2=拒绝、4=略低于、6=略高于、8=接受、10=强烈接受)。 • 信心使用5级(1=无法评估,5=绝对确定)。 ^ 盲目检查 询问审查者是否认为该条目是2026年的正文,是AI生成的建议书,还是他们无法透露.

blocks.en: All four methods run the same loop. This section specifies that loop and then the profile and actions each method changes.
blocks.zh: 所有四种方法运行同一回路. 本节指定了循环,然后是每个方法改变的配置和动作。

blocks.en: C.1 Shared Agent Loop
blocks.zh: C.1 共享代理循环

blocks.en: For LLM agents, an agent harness provides the interface through which a language model observes and acts in an environment. Our harness follows ReAct ( Yao et al., 2022 ) , interleaving reasoning, actions, and observations in the model’s prompt, similar tool-based interaction loops supporting research planning in Idea2Plan ( Huang et al., 2025a ) , idea generation in The AI Scientist-v2 ( Yamada et al., 2025 ) , and skill learning ( Zhong et al., 2026a ) . In our setting, one run of the LLM agent within this harness produces a single proposal. The harness provides the agent with a profile, a step budget, and a set of available actions. The agent follows the ReAct loop, deciding for itself which actions to take and how to spend the budget.
blocks.zh: 对于LLM代理来说,一种代理牵引提供了语言模型在环境中观察和行动的界面. 我们的利用遵循ReAct(Yao等,2022年),在模型的即时,类似基于工具的交互循环中交互推理、行动和观察,支持Idea2Plan(Huang等,2025a年)的研究规划,在"AI科学家-v2"(山田等,2025年)中的思想生成,以及技能学习(Zhong等,2026a年). 在我们的环境下,一个LLM代理 运行在这个渠道里 产生一个单一的建议。 该工具为代理人提供了简介、一步预算以及一套可用的行动。 代理人遵循ReAct循环,自行决定采取什么行动以及如何花出预算.

blocks.en: Every response carries exactly one tagged action, and every step costs one unit of a budget of at most 20 model calls. plan records the current working hypothesis and replaces the previous plan. search takes a query with an optional publication-year filter and runs the hybrid retrieval above over the area’s corpus. read_papers pins retrieved documents into a working set of 50 cards, evicting the least recently requested card when the set is full. draft replaces the working draft. summary condenses the agent history into notes that replace it, leaving the working set intact. proposal submits and ends the agent loop. Figure C.1 gives the prompt that defines them.
blocks.zh: 每一次答复都包含一个贴有标签的行动,每个步骤花费一个单位的预算,最多20个模式呼叫。 计划记录当前的工作假设,并取代先前的计划. 搜索时使用可选的出版年过滤器进行查询,并在区域目录上运行混合检索。 read_papers pins 将文档检索到50张卡片的工作组合中,当套片满后,将最近要求的最小的卡片驱逐出. 草案取代工作草案。 摘要将代理历史压缩成可替换它的注释,使工作集完好无损. 提交并结束代理循环。 图C.1给出了定义它们的提示.

blocks.en: System You are a research scientist preparing ONE new research proposal. Your research community is defined as: <the area’s definition, as given in Table 5 > The literature you can access ends at 2025-12-31. You don’t need to finish in one step --- you may plan, search, read, draft and revise across multiple steps, one action per step. You will be provided with: 1. Your researcher profile. 2. Your pinned papers --- the full cards you pinned with < < read_papers > > , listed in the order you pinned them, with the count at the end of the block. Nothing is ever lost: the corpus does not change, so any [CAND] id you have seen can be pinned back and its full card reappears here. 3. Your history --- an append-only log of what you did, one entry per step, in the order it happened. A < < search > > entry is followed by its < < information > > block (which opens with a receipt counting new vs. already-retrieved results); a < < read_papers > > entry is followed by a receipt; a < < plan > > or < < draft > > entry records only that you rewrote it --- the text itself lives in your workspace. Past steps are never rewritten --- only a < < summary > > replaces the earlier entries wholesale. In the history every [CAND] result is a title-only line; a line marked ’(shown above)’ is one that appeared earlier. 4. Latest search results --- the full cards of your most recent search. Once you search again this block is replaced, so pin anything you want to keep reading. 5. Your workspace --- what you are writing: your latest < < plan > > , your latest < < draft > > , and any < < feedback > > . A < < summary > > clears the plan and the draft but keeps your pinned papers, which is why that action asks you to carry them into your notes. 6. Your remaining step budget (each response consumes one step). IMPORTANT: You must strictly adhere to the following rules: 1. Choose ONLY ONE action from the list below for each response, DO NOT perform more than one action per step. 2. Follow the exact syntax format for the selected action, DO NOT create or use any actions other than those listed. 3. The corpus is a bounded snapshot of one research community. Thin or empty results mean "not found in this corpus", NOT proof that no such work exists anywhere; ground research-gap claims in the papers you actually retrieved and cited. 4. Form a hypothesis early and let evidence attack it. Put a first < < plan > > on the table within your first few steps, then use < < search > > to test it --- searching is how you check, refute or sharpen your idea. 5. The episode ends when you output < < proposal > > , and you may output it on any step. "Steps remaining: 1" is the deadline: your response then MUST be the < < proposal > > , otherwise the episode ends with nothing. 6. Every id in your References section MUST be a paper you actually retrieved: copy it verbatim from a [CAND] line anywhere in your history --- search results, your working set, or ids you kept in your summary notes. You are NOT allowed to invent ids or cite papers that never appeared. List each paper at most once. 7. Cite inline with bracketed numbers [1], [2], ... matching your References entries. The same paper always reuses the same number. Do NOT write raw [CAND] ids inside the prose --- they belong only in the References section. 8. The proposal must be concrete and technically grounded: a specific falsifiable core idea, not a survey or a vague direction. It must be new relative to the literature you retrieved, and your proposal must say exactly what is new: in its related-work discussion, name the closest papers you found and state what your proposal does that they do not --- a different problem framing, a different mechanism, a different evaluation that would settle something they left open. Restating or incrementally tuning a retrieved paper is not a proposal. Every proposal has related work: if you found none, that almost always means the search was too narrow, not that the idea is unprecedented --- claim the latter only if you are prepared to defend it. Claim novelty only against what you actually retrieved and cited (see rule 3). Valid actions: 1. < < plan > > research state < < /plan > > : your current working hypothesis and anything else worth carrying forward --- including but not limited to (a) the idea you are proposing, stated as a specific falsifiable claim; (b) what would show it is wrong, already done, or not worth doing; (c) a finding, a constraint you hit, or a question to settle later. A rough hypothesis on little evidence is fine and expected. Issue < < plan > > again to replace it: sharpen it as evidence accumulates, and when evidence kills it --- the claim is wrong, or the retrieved literature already does it --- move to a different gap instead of defending it. Apart from your < < draft > > , this is the only note that survives into the next step. 2. < < search > > query < < /search > > : search the local literature corpus (a short natural-language or keyword query, < < = 25 words). Optionally append a publication-year filter after a pipe, e.g. < < search > > repository level code generation | years: 2020-2025 < < /search > > (a single year also works). The engine combines keyword (BM25) and semantic matching. 3. < < read_papers > > id1, id2, ... < < /read_papers > > : pin papers you have already retrieved into your < < working_set > > --- use it to read a paper whose card has been compressed to a title-only line, or to keep an important one in full while you work. Copy the ids verbatim from [CAND] lines. The working set holds 50 cards; when it is full the least recently requested one is evicted. A card carries the paper’s metadata and its abstract --- the corpus has no full text, so the abstract is all there is of a paper’s content. 4. < < draft > > revised or newly written working draft of your proposal < < /draft > > : write or revise your working draft based on what you have learned --- this is where your < < plan > > hypothesis becomes an actual proposal. The latest draft replaces the previous one. Ideally you start drafting while 5-10 steps remain, so there is room left to sharpen the proposal rather than writing it in the last step. 5. < < summary > > research notes < < /summary > > : condense your history into notes. Keep the plan, the current draft state, key findings, and the [CAND] ids you may still want to cite (one line per id is enough --- you can pin any of them back into your working set later with < < read_papers > > ). Your subsequent history will be replaced by this summary; your < < working_set > > is preserved automatically. 6. < < proposal > > final proposal in markdown < < /proposal > > : output the final proposal as a self-contained markdown document: - First line: "# < < specific title > > ". - Then a paragraph starting with "**Abstract**: " --- 4-8 sentences summarizing the whole proposal (this is what the community will first see). - Then a related-work section: the closest papers you retrieved, named, and what your proposal does that they do not. - Then the rest of the proposal body in free-form prose, structured however serves the idea best. A strong proposal covers: motivation, the research gap that follows from the related work, the core idea (crisp and falsifiable), method, implementation plan, experiment plan (datasets, baselines, metrics, ablations), and expected contribution --- but the organization, depth, and voice are yours. - Cite inline with [1], [2], ... throughout the body. - End with a "## References" section, exactly one line per cited paper, in the format: [n] < < the id copied from the [CAND] line, WITHOUT any brackets around it > > | role: method|baseline|motivation|extension|background | one sentence on how this paper is used For example: [1] D3f2a9c01d2e4 | role: baseline | We compare against this retrieval-augmented generator. Format: use exactly one tag pair per response --- < < plan > > , < < search > > , < < read_papers > > , < < draft > > , < < summary > > , or < < proposal > > . No text outside the tags.

blocks.en:
The areas named in topic profiles come from the topic labels already carried by OpenAlex records. The set of topics itself was built from the citation network. OpenAlex started with works that have incoming and outgoing citations and clustered them by citation relationships ( OpenAlex, 2024 ; van Eck, 2024 ) .
We collect topic label on a ≤ 2025 \leq 2025 paper, and we weight topics by an exponential decay in publication year with a half-life of two years, which favors recent practice without cutting the earlier years off. The resulting distribution is allocated across the population by largest remainder. As shown in Table 15 , topics read like Topic Modeling, Machine Learning in Materials Science, Scientific Computing and Data Management, and Multi-Agent Systems and Negotiation. Some topics look unrelated to the specific research area, but the topic allocation is a rough guide to the areas the LLM agent is expected to explore, and it does not constrain the search or the proposal. The LLM agent may search for any topic in the corpus and propose any idea it can justify. At a population of 300 the allocation reaches between 146 and 177 distinct topics out of the several thousand that carry prior mass.

我们在2025\leq 2025年的论文上收集主题标签, 我们把主题放在出版年份的指数衰减, 半衰期为两年, 由此造成的分布按最大部分的剩余人口分配。 如表15所示,题目为专题建模、材料科学中的机器学习、科学计算和数据管理以及多代理系统和谈判。 有些专题看起来与具体研究领域无关,但专题分配是LLM代理人预期会探索的领域的粗略指南,并不限制搜索或建议. LLM代理人可以搜索本文书中的任何主题,并提出它可以证明的任何想法。 在300名人口中,分配额达到146至177个不同的题目,其中几千个题目具有先前的质量。

blocks.en: The tags behind landscape are extracted from the 2025 papers. A language model with prompt as shown in Figure C.2 reads one paper at a time and names the task it addresses and the method it uses, drawing on a tag set that starts empty and grows as papers are processed in publication order. After each batch a second pass merges newly proposed tags into existing entries. A final pass by hand merges the variants that survive, such as modifier and hyphen differences and the same name appearing on both axes. In automated research this yields task tags such as autonomous experimentation, equation discovery, AI scientist, and scientific hypothesis generation, and method tags such as llm agent, multi-agent system, benchmark construction, and retrieval-augmented generation.
